questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. **

They never ________ those who have done wrong.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4), i.e., Forgive.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c85df1d0885ef6fd1ccb6d6eeeb4f0ac2cb3339955502df2aa31deb31b5ead58.png] **Explanation**:

The blank is used right after the adverb '**never**', suggesting that it should contain a verb.

*Given the context, the verb should mean 'blame' or alternately, 'excuse'. Both can fit here.*

**Let's look at the meanings of the given options:**

**Conduit**- a channel for conveying water or other fluid.

**Outcast**- a person who has been rejected or ostracized by their society or social group.

**Contain**- have or hold (someone or something) within.

**Forgive**- stop feeling angry or resentful towards (someone) for an offence, flaw, or mistake.

Out of these, only **Forgive **fits the context of 'those who have done wrong'.

**Thus, the complete sentence is:** *They never* **forgive*** **those who have done wrong.*

questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Does he like to go for sight seeing when he is in holiday?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3),i.e., In holiday?**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c85df1d0885ef6fd1ccb6d6eeeb4f0ac2cb3339955502df2aa31deb31b5ead58.png] **Explanation**:

__
 
• The error lies in option 3, which uses the incorrect preposition '**In**'.
 
• **In**- expressing the situation where something is surrounded by something else. ***Example: I am in Hawaii.***
 
• Given the context, the preposition should be showing the state of his being engaged in 'a holiday'.
 
• ** Important Point:**
 
• So, the correct preposition here should be '**On**'.
 
• **On**- indicating the state or process that one is engaged in. ***Example: The officer was on leave when it happened.***

**Thus, the rectified sentence is: ***Does he like to go for sight seeing when he is **on holiday?***

*** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] Hinglish__** *

 
• त्रुटि option 3 में है, जो गलत पूर्वसर्ग '**In**' का उपयोग करता है।
 
• **In**- उस स्थिति को व्यक्त करना जहां कोई चीज किसी और चीज से घिरी हो। **उदाहरण:** ***I am in Hawaii. (***मैं हवाई में हूँ।***)***
 
• संदर्भ को देखते हुए, पूर्वसर्ग को 'छुट्टी' में लगे होने की स्थिति को दर्शाना चाहिए।
 
• **Important Point:**
 
• तो, यहाँ सही पूर्वसर्ग '**On**' होना चाहिए।
 
• **On**- उस प्रक्रिया को इंगित करना जिसमें कोई लगा हुआ है। **उदाहरण:** ***The officer was on leave when it happened. (***घटना के वक्त अधिकारी छुट्टी पर थे।***)***

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement. **

A Study has shown that the use of mobile data in India __have increased 50 times__ over the last three years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2), i.e., Has increased 50 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a9d568b6419aa6ff37bbc42d94c53d413184d6cf8d7840be45cac8c3a302863.png] **Let's look at the following points-**

__
 
• The sentence uses the incorrect plural verb '**have increased**'.
 
• The subject of the verb is the singular '**use**'.
 
• ** Important Point: **
 
• ** Subject Verb Agreement Rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb; while a plural subject requires a plural verb. *Example: She talks. (Singular); They talk. (Plural).***
 
• Here, the singular subject '**Use**' requires the singular present perfect verb '**Has increased**'.

 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d407e393fc273aca07f0a376b0337bc9a3bd769df6ce218173eeb8b6ab61fd95.png] Confusion Point-**

 
• Option 3, '**has been increased to 50 times'** is grammatically correct; but using 'To' requires a comparative noun in order to be meaningful. (Increased to 50 times of what?)
 
• So, in order to be correct, the structure would be: Increased to 50 times (of) the original value. 

**Thus, the rectified sentence is:** *A Study has shown that the use of mobile data in India **has increased 50 times__** over the last three years.*

To keep an eye on
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1, i.e., To keep a watch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• To keep an eye on means keep under careful observation.

 
 
• * Example: The jury asked the police to keep an eye on the convict.*
 
 
 
• The phrase is derived from the attention that is given by a person to a task at hand, which requires him to 'keep his eye on' the given task.

• *उदाहरण: The jury asked the police to keep an eye on the convict.*
